title: Adaptive prefetch pipeline for model KV profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a data-driven pipeline that computes model-specific prefetch and KV retention recommendations based on observed sequence prefix characteristics and runtime latency/cost trade-offs. The pipeline should take per-model request traces, cluster sequence shapes, run lightweight microbenchmarks to measure marginal token cost and latency for different prefetch window sizes, and produce an artifact (KV prefetch profile) that the onboarding flow can publish to the model catalog. This is intended to reduce tail latency for long-context workloads while keeping token cost predictable and enabling safe version assignments in the pinning workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline produces a stable KV prefetch profile artifact for at least 10 open-source models in the catalog with metadata: model_version, sequence_clusters, recommended_prefetch_window, expected_token_delta, expected_p99_latency_change
Profiles are stored in the model catalog and referenced by the onboarding UI; publishing toggles are available (manual review / auto-publish), and a 7-day retention is supported for profile diffs

End-to-end test: deploying recommended prefetch to a canary pool shows <=3% increase in median latency and >=12% reduction in 99th percentile latency for sampled long-context customer traces compared to baseline (no prefetch), measured in the benchmark dashboard
Integration with version pinning: when a model version is pinned, the onboarding flow locks the prefetched-window field and records the profile hash in the version metadata
Regression guardrails: alerting when production observed metrics deviate >25% from predicted profile estimates (latency or cost), with links to trace ids for root cause
tasks: Define sequence clustering feature set and implement offline clusterer job (data team)
Create microbenchmark runner that tests a range of prefetch window sizes and records per-token latencies and KV cache hit rates
Design profile schema and storage layout in model catalog (artifact spec + versioning)
Add publish workflow in onboarding UI with preview diff and reviewer approvals
Add canary rollout automation to apply profile to a small subset of requests and collect validation metrics
Add dashboard panels: profile predictions vs observed, per-model sample traces, and alert rules
Write unit/integration tests and an end-to-end benchmark harness
proposal_notes: We observed that many long-context customers exhibit a bimodal sequence-length distribution: short interactive bursts and occasional long-document uploads. A static prefetch window wastes tokens for the short bursts. The adaptive pipeline will recommend a profile that favors small prefetch for the primary cluster and a larger window for the long-tail cluster, plus suggested KV retention TTLs. We'll start with a simple cost-latency optimizer that scores windows using a weighted objective (alpha * latency_p99 + beta * token_cost). Alpha/beta will be configurable per-customer tier.
decisions: Start with offline profiling (no runtime ML) and deterministic heuristics for mapping clusters -> prefetch window
Publish profile artifacts as immutable, content-addressed blobs so onboarding can reference profile hashes in pin metadata
Expose alpha/beta weights in the console under 'Optimize for' with options: latency-focused, cost-balanced, cost-focused
risks: Profiles could be stale if request mix changes rapidly; mitigation: schedule recurrent profiling and add profile age to onboarding warnings
Incorrect cluster assignments might recommend harmful prefetch sizes; mitigation: require manual sign-off for P0 customers and run small canaries before full rollout
Telemetry volume & privacy: need to ensure sampling respects PII rules and enterprise customers can opt out
